subject.title: [Feature]: Browser sandbox should support non-Docker backends (external CDP/noVNC endpoint)

question: Should OpenClaw add a narrow sandbox-browser external CDP/noVNC endpoint contract now, fold this into a broader browser-backend Plugin SDK design, or keep Docker-managed sandbox browsers as the only supported path for now?
rationale: The request changes public config and browser-control security boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the endpoint trust, auth, lifecycle, noVNC, and SSRF contract.

options.title: Design narrow external endpoint contract
options.body: Add explicit sandbox-browser endpoint config with validation, auth/noVNC/SSRF rules, docs, and tests while keeping Docker behavior unchanged.

options.title: Fold into broader browser backend API
options.body: Keep this issue linked to the broader browser-backend registry design and implement external sandbox browsers only through that approved seam.

options.title: Keep Docker-only for now
options.body: Leave sandbox-browser lifecycle Docker-managed until a stronger security model for external browser control is agreed.

recommendation.title: Design narrow external endpoint contract
recommendation.body: Add explicit sandbox-browser endpoint config with validation, auth/noVNC/SSRF rules, docs, and tests while keeping Docker behavior unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across sandbox browser SSRF policy, current review context, and security-sensitive browser/sandbox boundaries.
